title: Keel cannot raise its own rate limits: writing them is admin-only, spending them is controller-only, and reading them is public
content:
The Rate Limit Management section splits three ways. `setRateLimitData(...)` is declared `public override onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE)` (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.3.2); `triggerRateLimitDecrease(...)` is `external override onlyRole(CONTROLLER)` (…3.5); and of both read functions the text says plainly "anyone can query" (…3.1, …3.4).

Since "the rate limit configuration serves as whitelisting," admin-only writes mean Sky Governance — which holds `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` via the Keel Proxy — decides both which venues Keel may touch and how much it may move. Keel's tokenholders vote to *propose* an allocation Instance; the limit that makes it operable is set one level above them. An Agent under pressure cannot widen its own constraints.

The controller-only decrement is the matching restriction on the other side: capacity is consumed only through the Controller's own accounted operations, never adjusted by an operator directly, so consumption always corresponds to a real action that emitted an event.

Public reads complete the arrangement. Keel's remaining headroom on every limit is world-readable state, so KEEL holders, partners and the Freezer signers can all see how close the Agent is running to its ceilings without asking Keel. Combined with the `RateLimitDataSet` and `RateLimitDecreaseTriggered` events, both the budget and its consumption are externally monitorable in real time.
description: setRateLimitData carries onlyRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) and triggerRateLimitDecrease onlyRole(CONTROLLER), while getRateLimitData and getCurrentRateLimit are open to anyone.
